 Traffic bans for trucks in Europe
 2026-10-26 Germany: Truck driving bans at the end of October and beginning of November 
 On 31 October, the public holiday truck ban will apply in nine German federal states, while on 1 November it will cover the whole of Germany because All Saints’ Day falls on a Sunday. Exceptions are provided for both days, including certain journeys in Lower Saxony, transport to and from Berlin, and traffic in North Rhine-Westphalia. 
 Under Section 30 of the German Road Traffic Regulations (StVO), the Sunday and public holiday ban applies from 00:00 to 22:00. It covers trucks with a gross vehicle weight exceeding 7.5 tonnes and trailers to trucks used for the commercial or paid carriage of goods, including empty journeys associated with such transport.
 31 October - Reformation Day
The public holiday ban applies in Brandenburg, Bremen, Hamburg, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Lower Saxony, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, Schleswig-Holstein and Thuringia.
In Lower Saxony, the ban starts at 06:00. Until 22:00, transit is permitted on the following designated motorway sections:
➡️ A1: Lotte/Osnabrück - Osnabrück-Nord
➡️ A2: Bad Oeynhausen - Lower Saxony/Saxony-Anhalt border
➡️ A30: Bad Bentheim - Bad Oeynhausen
➡️ A31: Schüttorf - Lower Saxony/North Rhine-Westphalia border
➡️ A33: Osnabrück-Süd - Dissen-Süd
 Exemption for journeys to and from Berlin
On 31 October, from 00:00 to 22:00, journeys to and from Berlin are permitted on designated motorway sections in Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia. The exemption covers trucks with a gross vehicle weight exceeding 7.5 tonnes and trucks with trailers.
The list of motorways covered by the exemption includes A2, A4, A9, A10, A11, A12, A13, A14, A15, A17, A19, A20, A24, A38, A71, A72, A73, A111, A113, A114, A115, A117 and A143. The exemption applies only to the specified sections, not the entire length of these motorways, and does not permit unrestricted transit through the listed states.
In Brandenburg, journeys along designated routes to and from logistics centres in Wustermark, Freienbrink and Großbeeren, as well as Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER), are also permitted.
 1 November - Ban throughout Germany
On Sunday, 1 November, the ban will apply nationwide. All Saints’ Day is also a public holiday in Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland. In the other federal states, the ban will apply because it is Sunday.
 Exemption in North Rhine-Westphalia
North Rhine-Westphalia has a special exemption issued in 2026, providing for two sets of exceptions:
● 00:00-06:00 - journeys related to the transport of goods within the state are permitted, including associated empty runs.
● 06:00-22:00 - transit is permitted on designated sections of motorways A1, A2 and A30 near the border with Lower Saxony.
The regulation remains in force until 31 December 2030 and also applies when 1 November falls on a Sunday.
